tools.name: Claude Code
tools.description: Official Claude Code CLI — the runtime every plugin in this repo executes inside.
features: skills (SKILL.md frontmatter: name, description, model, allowed-tools, disable-model-invocation)
subagents (agents/*.md; plugin-qualified names required for context: fork)
context: fork routing a skill body into a named subagent
tools.notes: THE breaking-change surface for this repo. Watch specifically: (1) skill frontmatter field additions/renames — every SKILL.md here depends on them; (2) `context: fork` + `agent:` name resolution semantics — a silent-fallback regression already burned this repo once (bare agent name ran promptless on the session model, 2026-07-17); (3) subagent frontmatter allow/deny list — hooks/mcpServers/permissionMode are blocked for plugin subagents, that list can change; (4) marketplace manifest schema; (5) model aliases in `model:` fields (haiku/sonnet/opus). CHANGELOG.md in the repo root is the signal, not the release tags.

tools.name: Anthropic Skills
tools.description: Anthropic's official Agent Skills collection + the Agent Skills spec and template.
features: production document skills (PDF/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX) as reference implementations
installable as a Claude Code plugin marketplace
Skills API (upload custom skills via Claude API)
tools.notes: De-facto authority on skill authoring convention. `spec/` is the one to watch — a spec change is a compatibility change for every SKILL.md in this repo. Also a quality benchmark: their skills show how Anthropic itself handles progressive disclosure and supporting-file layout, which is exactly the pattern devil-review uses (methodology.md / output-schema.md / domains/*.md siblings). Works across Claude Code, claude.ai and the API — if this repo's plugins ever need to run outside Claude Code, this is the portability spec.

tools.name: claude-code-templates
tools.description: Large catalog of agents, commands, hooks, MCPs, settings and skills for Claude Code, installed via npx.
features: agents, slash commands, skills, hooks, settings, MCP configs
npx installer with per-component selection (--agent development-team/frontend-developer)
tools.notes: The breadth competitor: quantity and discoverability, not depth. Its real differentiator over this repo is the DISTRIBUTION layer — a web catalog and a per-component npx installer, versus `/plugin marketplace add`. Watch for: component-level install (grab one skill, not a whole plugin), and whether they add versioning/changelog discipline (they currently don't do lockstep manifests the way this repo does). Not a methodology competitor — no equivalent to devil-review's schema/evals discipline.

tools.name: superpowers
tools.description: A full software-development methodology packaged as composable skills — the closest philosophical competitor to devil-review.
features: brainstorming → design approval → planning → subagent dev → code review → branch completion workflow
parallel agent dispatch + git worktree management skills
installs on 11 harnesses (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity, Factory Droid, ...)
tools.notes: The one to actually watch. Same bet as this repo — methodology-as-skill, 'systematic over ad-hoc', 'evidence over claims' — at ~9x the star count. Two things it does that this repo does not: (1) MULTI-HARNESS install, one methodology across 11 agents; (2) a code-review skill inside a full lifecycle workflow rather than standalone. Its code-review skill is the direct devil-review comparison point — check how it handles verification and false positives. Conversely this repo's differentiators to defend: versioned output schema, eval suite guarding prose rules, adversarial verification pass. If superpowers ships a versioned schema or evals, the moat narrows.

tools.name: wshobson/agents
tools.description: Multi-harness plugin marketplace: 94 plugins / 203 agents / 175 skills authored once, transpiled per harness.
features: one source-of-truth plugins/ dir compiled to 5 harness-native formats (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini)
tiered model strategy per task criticality (Fable 5 / Opus / Sonnet / Haiku)
plugin-eval quality framework: static checks, LLM judge, Monte Carlo runs
tools.notes: Structurally the nearest neighbour to this repo — same marketplace shape, same per-plugin manifest idea, but two disciplines further along. `plugin-eval` (static + LLM judge + Monte Carlo) is a direct superset of this repo's evals/ approach; worth reading before extending the eval suite. Their tiered model strategy is the same reasoning as this repo's Pattern 1/2/3 model selection, made explicit per-task. The multi-harness transpile (8KB caps for Codex, TOML for Gemini) is the interesting structural idea: it means harness-specific constraints get encoded once. Watch the eval framework and the orchestrator pattern.

tools.name: awesome-claude-code
tools.description: Curated awesome-list of Claude Code tools, skills, plugins and workflows.
features: categorized index of skills, plugins, agents, hooks, workflows
tools.notes: Not a product competitor — a discovery channel and an early-warning radar. New marketplaces show up here before they show up anywhere else, so it is the cheapest way to spot a rising competitor. Also a distribution lever this repo has not pulled: an entry for mralabs/claude-plugins is a PR, not a build. Signal to watch in its diffs is new ENTRIES, not releases — the repo tags rarely.

tools.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
tools.description: OpenAI's terminal coding agent — the rival harness whose extension model shapes cross-harness expectations.
tools.notes: Already indirectly relevant: this session's environment carries a codex plugin (codex:rescue / codex:codex-rescue subagent), so Codex is a runtime peer here, not only a competitor's product. The convention worth tracking is AGENTS.md — if it converges with or diverges from CLAUDE.md, the rule files under .claude/rules/ may need a portable twin. Also watch its skill/plugin story: both wshobson/agents and superpowers already transpile into Codex, meaning a Codex plugin format is becoming a real distribution target for methodology repos like this one.

tools.name: opencode
tools.description: Open-source terminal coding agent with a build/plan agent split and an open plugin surface.
features: build agent (write access) vs plan agent (read-only) mode split
tools.notes: Interesting for two design ideas rather than as a rival. First, the build/plan agent split is the same read-only-review boundary devil-review needs — a review skill that structurally cannot write is a stronger guarantee than an allowed-tools list. Second, it is fully open source, so its plugin/extension internals are readable in a way Claude Code's are not — useful when reverse-engineering how a harness ought to resolve subagent names or scope tools. Being a common transpile target for the multi-harness marketplaces makes it a plausible second distribution channel.

tools.name: Antigravity CLI
tools.description: Google's terminal agent, successor to Gemini CLI — shares the Antigravity 2.0 agent engine with the GUI.
features: multi-step reasoning, multi-file editing, tool calling, persistent history
TUI optimized for SSH / keyboard-driven work
shared core engine with Antigravity 2.0 GUI; session export both ways
bidirectional settings sync between CLI and GUI
tools.notes: Replaces google-gemini/gemini-cli, which Google announced as transitioning to this (gemini-cli discussion #27274) — track this repo, not gemini-cli. Very early: ~1.8k stars, ~38 commits on main, and no documented skill/plugin/MCP extension surface yet. That is precisely why it is worth watching: the extension model is still being decided, and superpowers already ships an Antigravity install path, so a plugin format landing here becomes a distribution question for this repo fast. Signal to watch: the first release that names skills, plugins, custom commands or MCP.
